translation_en: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The keys of the unseen are five: “Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour; He sends down rain; He knows what is in the wombs; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Aware”’ (31:34).

Abu al-Nu‘man narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed, ‘Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you’ (6:65), the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘I seek refuge in Your Face.’ Then it says, ‘or from beneath your feet’ (6:65), and he said, ‘I seek refuge in Your Face.’ Then it says, ‘or confuse you into factions and make some of you taste the violence of others’ (6:65). The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘This is easier’—or ‘This is less severe.’

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me: Ibn Abi ‘Adi narrated to us, from Shu‘bah, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When the verse, ‘They did not mix their faith with wrongdoing’ (6:82), was revealed, his Companions said, ‘Which of us has not done wrong?’ Then the verse, ‘Indeed, associating others with Allah is a tremendous wrong’ (31:13), was revealed.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Mahdi narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-‘Aliyah, who said: A cousin of your Prophet—I mean Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both—narrated to me, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘It is not fitting for a servant to say, “I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.”’

Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim informed us, saying: I heard Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘It is not fitting for a servant to say, “I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.”’

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to me: Hisham informed us that Ibn Jurayj informed them. He said: Sulayman al-Ahwal informed me that Mujahid informed him that he asked Ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Is there a prostration in Surah Sad?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’ Then he recited from ‘We bestowed’ through His words, ‘So follow their guidance’ (6:90), and then said, ‘He is among them.’ Yazid ibn Harun, Muhammad ibn ‘Ubayd, and Sahl ibn Yusuf added, from al-‘Awwam, from Mujahid: I said to Ibn ‘Abbas, and he replied, ‘Your Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was among those who were commanded to follow their example.’

‘Amr ibn Khalid narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, who said: ‘Ata’ said, ‘I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say, “May Allah fight the Jews! When Allah forbade them the fat of these animals, they melted it down, then sold it and ate its price.”’ Abu ‘Asim said: ‘Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us: ‘Ata’ wrote to me, ‘I heard Jabir,’ from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

Hafs ibn ‘Umar narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Abu Wa’il, from ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said, ‘No one has greater protective jealousy than Allah. For that reason, He has forbidden shameful deeds, both open and hidden. And nothing is more beloved to Him than praise, so for that reason He has praised Himself.’ I asked, ‘Did you hear this from ‘Abd Allah?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’ I asked, ‘Did he attribute it to the Prophet?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’

Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahid narrated to us: ‘Umarah narrated to us: Abu Zur‘ah narrated to us: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west. When people see it, everyone on earth will believe, but that will be when belief will not benefit a soul that had not believed before.’

Ishaq narrated to me: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west. When it rises and people see it, they will all believe, and that will be when belief will not benefit a soul.’ Then he recited the verse.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu Wa’il, from ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I asked, ‘Did you hear this from ‘Abd Allah?’ He replied, ‘Yes, and he attributed it to the Prophet.’ He said, ‘No one has greater protective jealousy than Allah. For that reason, He has forbidden shameful deeds, both open and hidden. And no one loves praise more than Allah, so for that reason He has praised Himself.’

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Amr ibn Yahya al-Mazini, from his father, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A Jewish man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with his face having been slapped. He said, ‘Muhammad, a man from your Ansari Companions slapped me in the face.’ The Prophet said, ‘Call him.’ They called him, and he asked, ‘Why did you slap his face?’ He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I passed by the Jews and heard him say, “By the One who chose Musa above mankind.” I said, “And above Muhammad?” Then anger seized me, and I slapped him.’ The Prophet said, ‘Do not claim that I am superior to the other prophets. On the Day of Resurrection, people will fall unconscious, and I will be the first to recover. Then I will find Musa holding one of the supports of the Throne. I will not know whether he recovered before me or was spared because of his swoon at the Mount.’

Muslim narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik, from ‘Amr ibn Hurayth, from Sa‘id ibn Zayd, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said, ‘Truffles are among the manna, and their water is a remedy for the eye.’

‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sulayman ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman and Musa ibn Harun narrated to us. They said: Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-‘Ala’ ibn Zabr narrated to us, saying: Busr ibn ‘Ubayd Allah narrated to me: Abu Idris al-Khawlani narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu al-Darda’ say: There was an exchange between Abu Bakr and ‘Umar, and Abu Bakr angered ‘Umar. ‘Umar left him in anger, so Abu Bakr followed him, asking him to seek forgiveness for him. ‘Umar would not do so, until he shut his door in Abu Bakr’s face. Abu Bakr then went to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. Abu al-Darda’ said: We were with him when the Messenger of Allah said, ‘As for this companion of yours, he has outstripped others.’ ‘Umar regretted what he had done, so he came, greeted the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and sat with him. He told the Messenger of Allah what had happened. Abu al-Darda’ said: The Messenger of Allah became angry, while Abu Bakr kept saying, ‘By Allah, Messenger of Allah, I was more in the wrong.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Will you leave my companion alone? Will you leave my companion alone? I said, “O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to all of you,” and you said, “You lie,” while Abu Bakr said, “You have spoken the truth.”’ Abu ‘Abd Allah said: ‘Ghāmara’ means he got ahead in doing good.

Ishaq narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The Children of Israel were told, “Enter the gate prostrating, and say, ‘Relieve us,’ and We will forgive your sins”’ (2:58). But they changed it: they entered crawling on their backsides and said, “A grain in a hair.”’

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah informed me that Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: ‘Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfah arrived and stayed with his nephew al-Hurr ibn Qays. He was among those whom ‘Umar kept close. The Quran reciters were among the members of ‘Umar’s gatherings and consultations, whether they were mature men or young men. ‘Uyaynah said to his nephew, ‘Nephew, you have standing with this ruler, so ask his permission for me to see him.’ He said, ‘I will ask his permission for you.’ Ibn ‘Abbas said: Al-Hurr asked permission for ‘Uyaynah, and ‘Umar granted it. When he entered, he said, ‘Son of al-Khattab, by Allah, you do not give us generously, nor do you judge fairly between us.’ ‘Umar became angry and was about to act against him. Al-Hurr said to him, ‘Commander of the Faithful, Allah Most High said to His Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, “Accept what is readily offered, command what is right, and turn away from the ignorant”’ (7:199). ‘This man is one of the ignorant.’ By Allah, ‘Umar did not go beyond that verse when al-Hurr recited it to him, for he was one who stopped at the limits of Allah’s Book.’

Yahya narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, concerning the verse, ‘Accept what is readily offered and command what is right’ (7:199). He said: Allah revealed it only concerning people’s manners.

‘Abd Allah ibn Barrad said: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us, from his father, from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Allah commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, to accept what is readily offered from people’s manners—or words to that effect.

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahim narrated to me: Sa‘id ibn Sulayman narrated to us: Hushaym informed us: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, about Surah al-Anfal. He said, ‘It was revealed concerning Badr.’ Al-shawkah: the boundary. ‘Murdafin’: one group following another. ‘Radafani’ and ‘ardafani’: he came after me. ‘Taste’: undergo and experience; this does not mean tasting with the mouth. ‘Fayarkumahu’: he gathers it together. ‘Sharrid’: scatter. ‘If they incline’ (8:61): they seek. ‘Yuthkhina’: he overcomes. Mujahid said: ‘Muka’an’ means putting their fingers into their mouths, and ‘tasdiyatan’ means whistling. ‘Li-yuthbituka’: to imprison you.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Warqa’ narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning the verse, ‘Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason’ (8:22). He said: They were a group of Banu ‘Abd al-Dar.

Ishaq narrated to me: Rawh informed us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Hafs ibn ‘Asim narrate from Abu Sa‘id ibn al-Mu‘alla, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was praying when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, passed by me and called me. I did not go to him until I had finished praying. Then I came to him, and he said, ‘What prevented you from coming? Did Allah not say, “O you who believe, respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you”’ (8:24)? Then he said, ‘Before I leave, I will teach you the greatest surah in the Quran.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, went to leave, and I reminded him. Mu‘adh said: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Khubayb, who heard Hafs, who heard Abu Sa‘id, a man among the Companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, narrate this. He said that it is, ‘Praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds,’ the seven oft-repeated verses.

Ahmad narrated to me: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Hamid—namely, the son of Kurdayd, the companion of al-Ziyadi—who heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Abu Jahl said, ‘O Allah, if this is truly the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment’ (8:32). Then these verses were revealed: ‘Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness. And why should Allah not punish them when they turn people away from the Sacred Mosque…’ (8:33–34), through the end of the verse.

Muhammad ibn al-Nadr narrated to us: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Mu‘adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Jahl said, ‘O Allah, if this is truly the truth from You, then rain stones upon us from the sky or bring us a painful punishment’ (8:32). Then these verses were revealed: ‘Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness. And why should Allah not punish them when they turn people away from the Sacred Mosque…’ (8:33–34), through the end of the verse.

Al-Hasan ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yahya narrated to us: Haywah narrated to us, from Bakr ibn ‘Amr, from Bukayr, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man came to him and said, ‘Abu ‘Abd al-Rahman, have you heard what Allah says in His Book: “If two groups of believers fight one another…” (49:9), through the end of the verse? What prevents you from fighting, as Allah mentions in His Book?’ He replied, ‘Nephew, I would rather be misled concerning this verse and not fight than be misled concerning the verse in which Allah Most High says, “Whoever kills a believer deliberately…” (4:93), through its end.’ The man said, ‘Allah says, “Fight them until there is no persecution”’ (8:39). Ibn ‘Umar replied, ‘We did that during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when Islam was small in number. A man would be persecuted for his religion: they would either kill him or bind him. Then Islam became widespread, and there was no more persecution.’ When the man saw that Ibn ‘Umar would not agree with what he wanted, he said, ‘What is your view of ‘Ali and ‘Uthman?’ Ibn ‘Umar replied, ‘What is my view of ‘Ali and ‘Uthman? As for ‘Uthman, Allah had pardoned him, but you disliked that Allah should pardon him. As for ‘Ali, he is the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and his son-in-law.’ He gestured with his hand and said, ‘This is his daughter—or his daughter is there, as you can see.’

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Bayan narrated to us that Wabarah narrated to him, saying: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr narrated to me: Ibn ‘Umar came out to us—or came to us—and a man asked, ‘What is your view of fighting during times of fitnah?’ He said, ‘Do you know what fitnah is? Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to fight the polytheists, and entering their ranks was fitnah. It is not like your fighting over kingship.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: When the verse, ‘If there are 20 patient men among you, they will overcome 200’ (8:65), was revealed, it was prescribed for them that one man must not flee before 10. Sufyan said on more than one occasion: that 20 must not flee before 200. Then the verse, ‘Now Allah has lightened it for you’ (8:66), was revealed, and it was prescribed that 100 must not flee before 200. Sufyan added on one occasion: The verse, ‘Urge the believers to fight: if there are 20 patient men among you…’ (8:65), was revealed. Sufyan said: Ibn Shubrumah said—and I think he meant—that commanding what is right and forbidding what is wrong is like this.

Yahya ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Sulami narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed us, saying: Al-Zubayr ibn Khirrit informed me, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When the verse, ‘If there are 20 patient men among you, they will overcome 200’ (8:65), was revealed, that was difficult for the Muslims, because they had been commanded that one man must not flee before 10. Then relief came, and He said, ‘Now Allah has lightened it for you and knows that there is weakness among you: if there are 100 patient men among you, they will overcome 200’ (8:66). He said: When Allah reduced the number required of them, their patience decreased in proportion to the reduction made for them.

Abu al-Walid narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara’, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The last verse revealed was, ‘They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the person who dies leaving neither descendants nor ascendants…’ (4:176), and the last surah revealed was Bara’ah.

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to me: ‘Uqayl narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab. Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman also informed me that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Abu Bakr sent me during that Hajj with a group of callers. He sent them on the Day of Sacrifice to announce at Mina that after that year no polytheist would perform Hajj and no one would circumambulate the House naked. Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman said: Then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib behind them and ordered him to announce Bara’ah. Abu Hurayrah said: ‘Ali announced with us to the people at Mina on the Day of Sacrifice the declaration of Bara’ah, and that after that year no polytheist would perform Hajj and no one would circumambulate the House naked.

‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us: ‘Uqayl narrated to me. Ibn Shihab said: Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent me during that Hajj with the callers. He sent them on the Day of Sacrifice to announce at Mina that after that year no polytheist would perform Hajj and no one would circumambulate the House naked. Humayd said: Then the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib behind them and ordered him to announce Bara’ah. Abu Hurayrah said: ‘Ali announced with us to the people at Mina on the Day of Sacrifice the declaration of Bara’ah, and that after that year no polytheist would perform Hajj and no one would circumambulate the House naked.
